slides.title: Data vs Information! 📊
slides.text: Data is raw facts and numbers without context, like test marks 90, 80, 70. Information is processed and organised data with meaning, like a report card with student names!
slides.spoken: Data is raw facts and numbers without context, like test marks. Information is processed and organised data with meaning, like a report card!

slides.title: Data Storage Units! 💾
slides.text: Computers measure data storage using special units! A bit is the smallest unit (0 or 1). 8 bits make 1 byte. Then come KB, MB, GB, and TB from smallest to largest!
slides.spoken: Computers measure data storage using special units! A bit is the smallest unit. Eight bits make one byte. Then come kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, and terabyte!

slides.title: RAM — Working Memory! ⚡
slides.text: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile working memory. It is super fast and holds your open apps, but it loses ALL data when the computer is turned off!
slides.spoken: RAM is volatile working memory. It holds your open applications, but it loses all data when the computer is turned off!

slides.title: ROM — Startup Memory! 🔒
slides.text: ROM (Read Only Memory) is non-volatile. It keeps its data safe forever without electricity! It stores the permanent startup instructions called the BIOS.
slides.spoken: ROM is non-volatile memory. It keeps its data safe forever without electricity and stores permanent startup instructions called the BIOS.

slides.title: Storage Devices & Cloud! ☁️
slides.text: Hard disks (HDD), Solid State Drives (SSD), USB flash drives, CDs, DVDs, and cloud storage keep our files safe for the long term. Cloud storage lives on the Internet!
slides.spoken: Hard disks, solid state drives, USB flash drives, CDs, DVDs, and cloud storage keep our files safe. Cloud storage lives on the Internet!

challenges.question: What is the DIFFERENCE between data and information?
challenges.answer: Data is raw facts without context, information is processed and organised data
options: Data is raw facts without context, information is processed and organised data
Data and information are exactly the same thing
Information is raw and data is processed
challenges.hint: Think: uncooked rice vs cooked biryani! Data is raw numbers, information has headings and meaning.
challenges.misconception: Data and information are NOT the same! Data is raw and unorganised (like 90, 80), while information is processed and has meaning (like a report card with student names).

challenges.question: What is the SMALLEST unit of data storage in a computer?
options: A bit (0 or 1)
A byte
A kilobyte
challenges.hint: Think of a single electric switch that is off or on (0 or 1). That is the smallest unit!
challenges.misconception: A bit is the smallest unit! A byte is made of 8 bits. Never confuse bit with byte.

options: A byte
A bit (0 or 1)

challenges.question: What is RAM and what happens to its data when the computer is turned off?
challenges.answer: RAM is volatile memory — all data is lost when power is off
options: RAM is volatile memory — all data is lost when power is off
RAM keeps data forever even without electricity
RAM is the same thing as a hard disk drive
challenges.hint: RAM is like a whiteboard! Fast to write on, but wiped clean when the power goes off.
challenges.misconception: RAM is VOLATILE memory! It needs constant electricity. When the power goes off, EVERYTHING in RAM disappears!

challenges.question: Which storage device has NO moving parts and uses flash memory chips?
options: SSD (Solid State Drive)
HDD (Hard Disk Drive)
Compact Disc (CD)
challenges.hint: An HDD has spinning platters. This modern drive has no moving parts and is super fast!
challenges.misconception: An SSD has NO moving parts and uses flash memory chips, making it much faster and tougher than an HDD with spinning platters!

options: HDD (Hard Disk Drive)
SSD (Solid State Drive)
